accuracy.evidence: Spellings forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty and ninety checked against the Oxford English Dictionary; the hyphen in compound numbers twenty-one to ninety-nine follows New Hart's Rules (OUP). The say() function in learn/word100_art.js builds every word from 0 to 100 from the ONES, TEENS and TENS tables, and the lab only accepts the card equal to say(n), so the right answers cannot drift from the rule. Place value (57 = 5 tens and 7 ones) matches the Year 2 programme of study. Parameterised answers 10*a+b, a, 10*a and b are whole numbers at every corner of a 2..9, b 1..9.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 2 slips: teen words read as tens (fourteen beside forty, twelve beside twenty, sixteen beside sixty, nineteen beside ninety in the tens-word scene; eighteen for 80 from the robot; challenge tag teen), the spellings fourty, fivety and ninty (FIX messages, robot sayings 1 and 5, m4), writing sixty-two as 602 (predict in the build scene, p4, challenge tag place), swapping the digits (p4, m6, challenge tag swap), a missing hyphen (robot saying 4, m5, challenge tag hyphen) and ordering words by length (fourteen v forty predict and order scene).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about two-part number words: rods of ten are matched to -ty words, a word is assembled from a tens card, a hyphen and a ones card under a rods-and-cubes model, a word is turned into rods and cubes by tapping a tens pile and a ones pile (with the mat to take pieces back), and words are ordered by value. flagnumword (1014, words to 20) uses ten frames, teen spellings and an 11-20 track; it has no hyphen, no tens words beyond twenty and no base-ten rods. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_word100.js under 30% similar to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the mapping by building: in the build scene the readout under the mat reads '6 tens and 2 ones = 62' as they tap, turns red with 'Too many tens: 7 tens is more than sixty-two' if they overshoot, and the success line says 'The tens word gives 6 tens and the ones word gives 2 ones'. In the join scene the label fills in as fifty-____ then fifty-seven, and a teen card gets 'fifteen is a teen word, between 13 and 19. Count the rods: 5 tens.'

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the scene disproves: 'Which word is 40?' (fourteen, which starts with four) before the tens words; 'How do we write sixty-two as a number?' (602, written as you hear it) before building it from 6 rods and 2 cubes; 'Which is bigger: fourteen or forty?' (fourteen, it is longer) before ordering. The finish line reveals the child's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with two tagged wrong answers each. why() returns six distinct messages: teen (teen words are 13 to 19, whole tens end in -ty), spell (forty has no u), place (sixty-two has two digits; 602 is six hundred and two), swap (the tens digit comes first, so 85 starts with eighty), hyphen (a hyphen joins the two words) and same (nineteen is 19, ninety is 90).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete numbers (57 is 5 tens and 7 ones; Forty has no u) and pass the family kid FK limit in validate_lessons.py; the adult text names tens, ones, digit, numeral, number word and hyphen and passes the adult limit. Canvas labels are dark on white or cream, and labels shrink to fit at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea: two parts said tens first, writing with a hyphen, -ty versus -teen, and the tricky spellings plus tens with no ones word and one hundred. The adult text gives the Year 2 requirement and key words, the word-to-digit mapping, five named mistakes with what to ask, and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrase and under 12% overlap with every lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots (dark theme) of every step at rest and part-way through Show me: the three word cards fill the width at about 110 x 85 px with 18 px bold words, the join scene keeps rods, the numeral 83, the label and two rows of cards on screen without overlap, the build scene has two half-width piles about 170 x 75 px, and the order scene uses a 2 x 2 grid above four slots. Every action also has a button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: each word card ('40 is forty', 'Tens word eighty', 'Ones word three'), + ten, + one, − ten and − one in the build scene, each word to order, and Right or Slip. Results and the running total are announced through c.say and the canvas aria-label; challenge feedback is a polite live region. Right and wrong are shown by a tick or cross and words, not colour alone. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
